title: Very early look at my first game 'The Empire Game'
author: blackskies69
selftext:
Introducing my first game! Empire Games is a RTS with 4x elements baked into it. There is city building, researching, governments, dooms day weapons, occult activities, black jack, aliens, and Kaiju because I'm ADHD and I like lots of stuff to do. A little over a month of work so far and I'm enjoying the progress and learning curve. 

Concept:

I wanted to make a conquest style RTS with smart units. I'm still working on the smart part, but these units can micro themselves to a degree. There is a promotion system that allows units to improve their thinking as they survive, so you are rewarded for keeping units alive and good micro with less overhead. Units can be promoted to officers who can command up to 12 units at a time and micro them as needed. I don't really have a good shot of this in the clip, and I'm still working on improving it. 

Game will feature a conquer the world style campaign that will have: Demons, robot dinosaurs, zombies, biological terrors, AI uprisings, and Aliens. It will take place over 4 chapters, and yes even the dialogue is written by AI. 

It will also feature a Virtual LAN multiplayer set up for easy self hosting of lobbies with one lobby open for anyone to join in. Still working on lobby sizes. Map will be a global map, feature multiple victory types, a score system, leaderboard, and whatever other scope creep I can cram into this game. 

Artwork:

For the artwork I went with the vibrant and immersive style you see before you. Bask in it's AI generated glory you heathens. I decided to go with a toy like design based off of 90's war toys, and for animations I used the same principle. Units pop apart as if made from plastic. 

Workflows:

  
Nano banana for artwork, meshy for models, and then tripo for animations. For coding I used the Claude desktop app. Atrocious I know. Not an IDE in sight. I created multiple chats using no real organization except for golden hashes I kept in the repository and in the project files so I could spin up multiple chats to work across the project at the same time. 

Release: 

Game will be released for free with some free open source license if I can pick one. My primary goal for this was just to try and make a game. I'll post a link to its github when I'm not ashamed of its state. 

Challenges:

Optimization took at least 3 days of testing and tweaking. Moving different processes to different cores and removing entire gameplay mechanics just to ensure smooth gameplay. It's not perfect but its a better than it was, and I feel its needing some input. 

Background:

I come from an IT background working mostly help desk, and I'm switching into game design not for money but because it's just something I enjoy.
